subject: TTFT probe results and protocol decision
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Chen <paul.chen@fastpay.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: TTFT probe results and protocol decision

Hi Paul / FastPay team — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps to get a pilot running: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Target TTFT: median around ~80ms, 95th ~160ms, 99th target <= 250ms for the primary checkout flow.
- Concurrent steady-state throughput target: 150 qps peak for the US-east region with expected 2x burst headroom.
- Client mix: mix of mobile web + single-page web apps; browser-based clients are important.
- Streaming requirement: you want chunked partial output for a progressive UX. Default preference on the call was SSE, but WebSocket multiplexing was discussed.

Preliminary probe numbers (attached): latency_probe_results.csv — 24h synthetic probe across our dev pool. Key observations:
- Median TTFT: 92ms (dev pool, cold cache spikes to ~350ms on new model containers).
- 95th: 185ms; 99th: 312ms (not yet within your 99th target).
- Packetization cadence we measured: 220–420ms depending on tokenization and chunk thresholds.

Proposed tactical decisions (we recommend these for the pilot):
1) Protocol: start pilot on SSE for browser clients to simplify client integration and avoid socket multiplexing on first pass. We'll add an opt-in WebSocket variant in pilot phase 2 for your mobile SDKs if multiplexing is needed.
2) Chunk cadence: target a 150–300ms cadence by enabling early-emission heuristics (emit on punctuation / token-count thresholds) — reduces perceived latency while keeping server-side batching efficient.
3) TTFT mitigation: enable warmstart pinned instances for high-traffic routes + prefix KV caching; add an initial 1–2 token priming to reduce cold-start overhead.
4) Concurrency/Throughput: pilot config sets per-pod concurrency soft limit to 80 requests; autoscaling policy to add pods at sustained 120 rps.
5) Acceptance test: 24h synthetic probe + 4-hour canary with real FastPay traffic; acceptance if 95th < 200ms and 99th < 300ms for the checkout route.

Next steps / asks from FastPay:
- Confirm whether SSE-only initial pilot is OK, or if you need WebSocket in week-1 of the pilot for mobile multiplexing.
- Share a representative production trace or anonymized sample load profile (qps shape + client mix).
- Confirm target pilot start window (we suggested Jan 10–14 in the call but flexible).

Attachments: latency_probe_results.csv (raw probe), streaming_protocol_matrix.xlsx (tradeoffs matrix).

I’ll loop in Karthik and Priyom to propose a pilot config and schedule a 30-min runbook review.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: TTFT probe results and protocol decision

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Protocol: our primary concern with SSE is mobile reliability and connection churn on spotty cellular. We prefer WebSocket for the mobile SDK (multiplexing is useful for the in-app flows), but SSE would be fine for desktop web. If you can provide an easy toggle in the pilot config, we can start with SSE for web and enable WS for mobile in the second week.

2) TTFT targets: the 99th being at ~312ms on dev is higher than we can tolerate for checkout — our internal bar for checkout is 99th <= 250ms. If warmstart + priming helps, great; want to ensure the pilot has aggressive warmstart and cache warming before canary.

3) Pilot timing: Jan 11 works for us to begin warmstart and a smoke run on Jan 12. Formal canary on Jan 13.

4) Compliance: we'll need a short note on connection-level encryption and session expiration behavior for the mobile WS case (our security/infra team will review).

I'll upload a representative trace to the Drive link you shared by next Mon. 

—Paul
Paul Chen
Director of Platform Engineering, FastPay
paul.chen@fastpay.io
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Chen <paul.chen@fastpay.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: TTFT probe results and protocol decision

Paul — thanks for the note. A few technical clarifications and an explicit fallback plan: 

- SSE vs WebSocket: agree with hybrid approach. Pilot config (attached pilot_config.yaml) will expose a feature flag at the route level. Default: SSE for web routes; WS for mobile if you opt-in. WS implementation will use a single logical stream per user session and include keepalive + per-connection rate limits to protect backend concurrency.

- Cold starts / warmstart: we propose a staged warmstart before canary: pre-provision N=3 warm workers for the primary route 48h before the canary window, then run a cache warm routine to push prefixes into KV cache. This should reduce 99th substantially.

- Chunk cadence: implement adaptive cadence: emit within 100–300ms window, but bias to punctuation and sentence-boundaries. Why: gives perceived instant feedback while allowing server to batch tokens across requests. We will also instrument per-chunk token counts (configurable threshold, default: 64 tokens).

- Concurrency settings: pilot_config.yaml will set pod concurrency soft limit to 80 and autoscale trigger at sustained 100 rps; we recommend an initial cap on parallel model execution to avoid OOMs at peak burst.

- Telemetry: we'll add a short tag to all pilot traces so we can compute TTFT percentiles by client type. Please ensure your SDK emits client_type=mobile/web in the initial handshake.

I attached pilot_config.yaml with the concrete values we discussed. Happy to walk through the runbook in the 30-min engineering session — propose Tue, Nov 30 10:00am PT for a technical run-through (we can move if that conflicts).

-Karthik

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: TTFT probe results and protocol decision

Paul — great, thanks for the quick response and for uploading the trace next week. Confirming decisions and next actions: 

Agreed pilot plan:
- Protocol: hybrid — SSE for desktop web by default; WebSocket available for mobile SDKs behind a route-level flag. Toggle will be set to SSE-only for week-1; WS opt-in for week-2.
- Chunk cadence: adaptive 100–300ms window, default token threshold 64.
- Warmstart: pre-provision warm workers + cache warming as Karthik outlined (48h prep).
- Concurrency/autoscale: soft per-pod concurrency 80; autoscale at sustained 100 rps; burst handling via warm pool.
- Acceptance: 24h probe + 4h canary. Acceptance targets: 95th < 200ms, 99th < 300ms.

Deliverables & timeline:
- By Nov 29: Karthik to share pilot_config.yaml (attached) and a short runbook.
- Nov 30, 10:00am PT: engineering runbook review (30m).
- By Jan 8: FastPay to provide representative trace / load profile.
- Jan 11–13: warmstart + smoke + canary (as proposed).
- Doc: sow_pilot_mpa.pdf attached — please sign the MPA if the pilot terms look good; DocuSign link is in the Drive folder.

Security note for your infra team: all traffic will be TLS 1.2+; WS uses wss:// endpoints and we enforce session timeouts and short-lived tokens. We’ll send a one-page security brief for the mobile WS flow this week.

If that all looks good I’ll create the HubSpot milestone and schedule the Nov 30 runbook session.

Regards —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
